title: Trying something new.
author: pikuray
selftext: Pictures are by chatGPT. To compare me full pixel art vs pixel art + "handdrawn" style. Do you think this style works? I really like #1.

comments.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
comments.body: Is the game turn based, or it's an action game and the mobs will meet up with your party? By looking at it, it seems to be the former (an JRPG) and I'd go with style #1 because it looks super cute. In the offchance I'm wrong and it's a game like vampire survivors, I'd go with style 4 because it's readable and you can actually see the surrounding.

replies.author: pikuray
replies.body: turn-based tile combat so not a lot of moving i'm guessing you would go with #1

comments.author: kirin1905
comments.body:
I also like 1.   
  
I would rank 1,2,4,3. 

Pixel Art definitely feels like it fits the vibe of the screenshot, feels most familiar art style for type of game.

comments.author: JakSilver00
comments.body: Mix things. I will say the characters and their icons look better as a cartoon comic style. The stats look better in pixel art, but not because they're pixel art, because they're bolder. Which is kind of the same thing with the command window. If you look at the scenery, you can tell that it's different primarily in the pixel art as well, because it looks cleaner. However, the characters and enemies don't look as good in pixel art, which seems to be what all of the backgrounds are trying to emulate. The actual dirt and grass looks better as the other three versus the pixel art, unless you're trying to make a cheerful game. If you look at the detail of the flowers, the brightness of the water, the gradient of the weapons. You can better choose what style to do each thing in, but this is just my opinion.

comments.author: walls99
comments.body:
Congrats on getting this far. Keep up the good work. 

As for the sprites, I like #2 better because to me they look may be slightly larger, but definitely more brighter/colorful than #1. If you can make the anime sprites in #1 as colorful as the #2 sprites,  I would go with #1's anime style. 

In #4 the background is way more colorful. The house, the trees, the ground, fence, water, flowers etc have way more detail. 

Honestly that's why I'm torn between #2 and #4. 

If you can combine the sprites from #2, into the background from #4, I think that would give the world more color. I realize that's a mix of anime sprites with pixel art background, but that's my opinion. 

If there's an order to pick

Sprites: 2>1>4>3
Background : 4>2=1>3. 

To me the background in 2 and 1 looks the same. 

Looking forward to seeing more progress. Good luck

comments.author: Sozerius
comments.body:
My opinion is:

Anime and cartoon/comic look unappealing because there is a sense of cheap graphics, like the gut reaction one might have to some mobile games

Minimalist/stylized looks good, like there may be some interesting depth here.

Pixel Art looks fitting and more real to the environment - I think the biggest thing here is how the characters compliment the environment. It matches the characters/vice versa so that it feels 'coherent.' And that lack of coherency is what makes the others look lesser. Also, the minimalist/stylized and pixel art styles are not as "chibi" on the face (the wide cheeks.) I personally find these chibi faces to summon impressions of mobile cash grab games without any substance. Pixel art games on the other hand summon the feeling of deep, meaningful and crafted worlds/experiences.

My point generally being that I think the background might need to be different to truly compliment the styles that are not pixel art, because even in those images, the background basically looks like a pixel art game.
